blocks.text: Quick verdict

FloppyData is the cheaper choice: $10 for 10 GB against $45 at NodeMaven's pay-as-you-go rate and $100 for 100 GB against about $220, with datacenter traffic on the same balance and a free anti-detect browser. NodeMaven is the better choice when IP reputation directly affects revenue, such as ad accounts, valuable social profiles and e-commerce sellers, because its IP Quality Filter, quality guarantee and longer track record reduce bans. Test FloppyData on low-value tasks before trusting it with important accounts.

NodeMaven and FloppyData both put residential and mobile traffic on a single balance and both court multi-account operators, but at very different prices. FloppyData charges a flat $1/GB and includes a free cloud anti-detect browser. NodeMaven charges $2.20-$4.50/GB but screens every IP for fraud signals before assignment, offers long sticky sessions and pays out for bad proxies. This comparison asks when NodeMaven's quality is worth paying for.

blocks.text: NodeMaven in 2026: what you get

NodeMaven is the quality-first option. Instead of handing out whatever IP the pool returns, it screens addresses in real time and lets you choose how strict the screening is. That matters most for account-based work such as social media management and multi-accounting, where a flagged IP can cost you an account. The price reflects it: $4.50/GB without a plan and $2.20/GB on monthly plans.

Strengths: IP Quality Filter screens IPs before you get them; Long sticky sessions for account work; Traffic rollover and cashback; Quality guarantee that pays for bad IPs. Weak spots: Smaller pool than mass-market networks; No datacenter proxies; Pay-as-you-go rate is double the plan rate.
FloppyData in 2026: what you get

FloppyData sells proxies the way prepaid phone plans sell minutes: one flat $1/GB balance that works across residential, mobile and datacenter pools. Static residential IPs start at $1.79 each in monthly bundles (20 for $49) with unlimited bandwidth. It is one of the cheapest ways into residential traffic, but it is a newer brand with less independent benchmarking than the established names.

Strengths: Flat $1/GB on any volume; One balance across residential, mobile and datacenter; Cheap static residential bundles with unlimited bandwidth; Free cloud anti-detect browser. Weak spots: Newer brand with limited independent testing; Pool-size claims disputed by some reviewers; Mixed customer-support reviews.
Pricing: NodeMaven vs FloppyData

NodeMaven charges $4.50/GB pay-as-you-go and $2.20/GB on monthly plans, with residential and mobile traffic on one balance. A $3.50 trial includes 750 MB. Unused traffic rolls over, and you earn up to 10% cashback on used traffic. ISP proxies start at $2.99 per IP with unlimited traffic.

FloppyData charges a flat $1/GB for rotating traffic, and the same balance works for residential, mobile and datacenter IPs. Static residential proxies are sold in monthly bundles from $1.79 per IP (20 IPs for $49), and static datacenter IPs from $0.79 per IP.

Buying 10 GB, you would pay about $10 with FloppyData and $45 with NodeMaven: a 78% saving in FloppyData's favour. For a 100 GB month, FloppyData costs about $100 while NodeMaven costs about $220, so FloppyData saves around 55%. The sticker price is only half of it. NodeMaven's unused traffic carries forward, while FloppyData's does not (check current terms), so if your usage swings from month to month NodeMaven can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

FloppyData does not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. NodeMaven lists '30M+ residential + 250K mobile' and FloppyData lists '65M+ claimed (disputed)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, NodeMaven lists 150+ countries and FloppyData lists 148 (residential). On targeting, NodeMaven offers country, region, city and ISP, while FloppyData offers country and city.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, NodeMaven offers rotating or long sticky sessions (multi-day), and FloppyData offers rotating or sticky sessions. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. NodeMaven: the quality filter matters less for high-rotation crawling. FloppyData: cheap, but with limited independent benchmarking. Let price and the countries you need decide.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. NodeMaven: workable, but you pay a premium for filtering you may not need. FloppyData: workable for light tasks. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: NodeMaven. NodeMaven has the edge here. Why: pre-screened, low-fraud-score IPs with long sticky sessions. How FloppyData compares: cheap static residential IPs and a free anti-detect browser.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: fine for light checks. With FloppyData: city targeting at a flat rate. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Ad verification and geo-testing: NodeMaven wins. The deciding factor for NodeMaven: good quality but a smaller pool. The limitation on the FloppyData side: limited targeting depth and published data.
Tight budgets: FloppyData wins. The deciding factor for FloppyData: a flat $1/GB on any volume. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: mid-priced on plans, expensive on PAYG.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB. FloppyData: No free trial; free browser extension for testing a few locations. Verification and payment rules differ too. NodeMaven: Standard. FloppyData: Light. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test NodeMaven and FloppyData before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle NodeMaven vs FloppyData faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB; FloppyData: no free trial; free browser extension for testing a few locations).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, NodeMaven comes out ahead in 2, FloppyData in 1, and 3 are ties. That makes NodeMaven the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: NodeMaven is strongest for social media and multi-account management, while FloppyData is strongest for small budgets and experiments. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
